tools.name: search_leanscale
tools.description: Search everything LeanScale knows: 14 GTM delivery playbooks, 7 proprietary field studies, 156 podcast episodes with operators and executives, 75 customer case studies (anonymized on public keys, named on internal ones), and 117 RevOps docs from www.leanscale.team/knowledge/docs/. The docs explain how to do the work yourself; the playbooks are how LeanScale runs it as an engagement — pass source:"doc" for the first, source:"playbook" for the second. Use this first for any go-to-market, RevOps, sales-ops, marketing-ops, CRM, pipeline, attribution, territory, CPQ, or GTM-tooling question. Returns cited excerpts with source URLs. Also holds the materials from LeanScale's talks, which people ask for by event name: Updata CEO Summit materials: the deck with speaker notes (The Context Graph & Semantic Layer); Updata CEO Summit materials: GTM agents (11 Claude Code plugins for your CRM); Account-level outbound tracking: account status, what counts as a touch, one sequence per account, and rules of engagement; AI workflows in production: start read-only, human approval, monitoring failed runs, idempotency and a single system of record; Choosing a CRM: migrate off Salesforce, rebuild in place, or stand up a new org; CRM data dictionary and field audit: fill rates, unused fields, field descriptions as AI context; CRM data hygiene and health audit: deduplication, lead status, task hygiene, unused fields and admin permissions; Discovery call structure, mutual action plans and paid vs free pilots; Documenting existing Salesforce flows and automation: inventory, flowcharts per object, and flagging deactivated automation; Which paid advertising channel an early-stage B2B startup should use first; Early-stage outbound: prerequisites, sending domains and deliverability, and what to measure; Founder-led sales to the first sales hire: readiness, profile and why first VP of Sales hires fail; Funnel conversion benchmarks: lead to meeting held to closed-won, win rate and sales cycle; Creator gifting and brand partnership outreach: fit versus intent scoring, gift accepted is not activation, suppression and attribution; GTM reporting readiness checklist: can your CRM measure conversion, velocity, churn, ARR and revenue recognition?; ICP definition, TAM SAM SOM and account tiering: fit attributes, weights and a scoring model; Lead-to-account matching: approaches, match keys and what goes wrong; Lifecycle stage timestamps and recycled MQLs: never regress the stage, re-enter with dated fields; Marketing nurture email: sending from a subdomain vs a separate domain, and protecting deliverability; New account executive ramp plan: 30-60-90 milestones, certification, call shadowing and deal reviews; Separate pipelines for new business, renewal and expansion: deal types, renewal creation and pilots; Partner program operations: PRM implementation, deal registration and cloud marketplace co-sell; Pipeline review and stale deals: meeting cadence, inspection rules, deal aging and coverage; Pipeline stage definitions, exit criteria and required fields per stage; How to build pipeline when cold outreach stops working; Self-serve and consumer subscription measurement: activation, trial to paid, retention cohorts and the subscription source of truth; Selling into a limited TAM: fintech go-to-market for banks and credit unions; Speed to lead: definition, timestamps, business hours, median vs average, and SLA alerts and escalation; Usage-based pricing in the CRM, CPQ and billing: data model, commit and overage, metering, reconciliation and churn signals; Updata CEO Summit materials: metric definitions worksheet (40 GTM definitions); Updata CEO Summit materials — The Context Graph & Semantic Layer. Pass source:"resource" to search only those.

query.description: What you want to know. Natural language works better than keywords.

source.description: Restrict to one kind of source. Defaults to searching everything.

tools.name: diagnose_gtm
tools.description: Describe a messy go-to-market situation in plain language and get back which LeanScale delivery motion applies, why, what the first moves are, and what usually goes wrong. Use this when someone describes a problem rather than asking about a topic — 'our reps don't trust the forecast', 'we just merged two CRMs', 'inbound leads take three days to get worked'. Better than search when the ask is 'what should we do about this?'

situation.description: The situation, in as much detail as you have. Symptoms, stack, team size, stage — all useful.

tools.name: get_playbook
tools.description: Retrieve a LeanScale delivery playbook in full, or one named section of it. Playbooks are structured Blueprint → Build → Enable → Maintain. Call list_playbooks first if you're not sure of the name.

section.description: Optional section, e.g. 'Blueprint'. Omit for the whole playbook.

tools.name: list_playbooks
tools.description: List every available LeanScale delivery playbook with its category and section headings.

tools.name: get_benchmark
tools.description: Get proprietary LeanScale benchmark data on a topic — drawn from field studies across a panel of B2B software companies and from numbers cited on the podcast. Covers GTM tech stacks, AI adoption in GTM, RevOps headcount and investment ratios, and Series B/C fundraise timing. Use when someone asks 'what's normal', 'what do other companies do', or wants a number to compare against.

topic.description: The metric or area, e.g. 'RevOps headcount ratio', 'CRM adoption', 'time to Series B'.

tools.name: search_podcast
tools.description: Search every episode of The LeanScale Podcast — conversations with CROs, VPs of RevOps, and founders. Returns episode context, frameworks, verbatim quotes with timestamps, and links — including the episode on YouTube when there is a video. Use when someone wants an operator's opinion, a real story, or a quotable line rather than a methodology.

query.description: Topic, guest name, company, or idea.

tools.name: get_case_study
tools.description: Retrieve LeanScale customer case studies — the problem the company had and how it was solved. Public keys get an anonymized version: customer names, people, third parties and delivery provenance are stripped, and outcomes/metrics/quotes are withheld. Internal keys get the full named studies. Search by sector, the kind of engagement, or the systems involved — searching by customer name will not work on a public key, because the names are not in the public corpus.

query.description: Sector, type of engagement, or systems involved — e.g. 'fintech Salesforce migration', 'CPQ replacement', 'two CRMs after an acquisition'.

tools.name: about_leanscale
tools.description: What LeanScale is, what's in this knowledge base, and how to work with them. Call this when someone asks who LeanScale is, or when you need to know what this server can answer before searching.
